name: Freed vs Nabla
title: Freed vs Nabla: AI Medical Scribe Comparison for Clinicians
description: Compare Freed and Nabla - two leading AI-powered medical scribes for clinical documentation. See differences in pricing, EHR integrations, ambient listening, and note types.

summary.bottom_line: Both Freed and Nabla are excellent AI medical scribes with ambient listening and automatic note generation. Freed offers more affordable transparent pricing starting at $39/month with 90+ language support. Nabla has stronger enterprise EHR integrations via SMART on FHIR, faster note generation (~5 seconds), and NEJM-validated outcomes, but requires custom pricing for most plans.

sections.heading: Freed vs Nabla: Overview
sections.content: Freed and Nabla are both AI-powered medical scribes that use ambient listening to automatically generate clinical documentation. They aim to reduce clinician burnout by eliminating the need for manual note-taking during patient encounters. Freed is a newer, more affordable option that works with any web-based EHR, while Nabla offers deeper enterprise integrations and has been clinically validated in peer-reviewed research.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Freed offers transparent, published pricing starting at $39/month for 40 notes or $79/month for unlimited notes. Nabla's pricing is not publicly disclosed and requires a demo, though third-party estimates suggest ~$119-239/month per provider. Freed also offers a 50% student discount. Both offer free trials, though Nabla has a free tier with limited features.

sections.heading: EHR Integration
sections.content: This is where the tools differ most. Freed uses a browser extension approach that works with any web-based EHR - you simply install the extension and it pushes notes with one click. Nabla has invested heavily in native integrations via SMART on FHIR, including Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), and athenahealth. Nabla's Nabla Connect feature provides bidirectional sync via iFrame embedding. For practices using major enterprise EHRs, Nabla's deeper integration may be preferable; for practices with diverse or smaller EHRs, Freed's universal approach is more flexible.

sections.heading: Clinical Features
sections.content: Both tools support ambient listening and dictation. Nabla generates notes in about 5 seconds and supports 55+ specialties, while Freed supports 30+ specialties with 90+ language support (useful for multilingual practices). Both support SOAP, DAP, and psychiatric intake notes, but Nabla also supports BIRP notes. For coding, Freed offers both ICD-10 and CPT suggestions, while Nabla provides ICD-10 and HCC coding but not CPT.

sections.heading: Clinical Validation
sections.content: Nabla has published peer-reviewed research in NEJM AI showing a 9.5% reduction in time-in-note at UCLA Health across 238 clinicians and 14 specialties. Freed has not published similar clinical validation studies. For organizations that prioritize evidence-based technology selection, this may be a meaningful differentiator.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your practice context:

recommendations.when: You want transparent pricing, need to work with any web-based EHR, serve multilingual patients (90+ languages), or are cost-conscious
You use a major enterprise EHR (Epic, Cerner, athenahealth) and want deep native integration, need BIRP notes, or your organization values peer-reviewed clinical validation
You need core ambient AI documentation with HIPAA compliance and standard note types

faqs.q: Which AI scribe is cheaper: Freed or Nabla?
faqs.a: Freed is more affordable with transparent pricing starting at $39/month. Nabla requires custom pricing but is estimated at $119-239/month per provider. For budget-conscious practices, Freed offers better value.

faqs.q: Does Freed or Nabla work better with Epic?
faqs.a: Nabla has deeper Epic integration through SMART on FHIR and joined the Epic Toolbox in October 2025. Freed works with Epic via browser extension but doesn't have the same native integration depth.
Freed supports 90+ languages compared to Nabla's 35+ languages. For practices serving diverse multilingual populations, Freed offers broader language coverage.

faqs.q: Are Freed and Nabla HIPAA compliant?
faqs.a: Yes, both are HIPAA compliant with BAA available. Both are SOC 2 Type 2 certified and do not use PHI to train their AI models. Nabla additionally has ISO 27001 certification.
Nabla advertises ~5 second note generation. Freed is described as 'fast' but doesn't publish specific timing. Both generate notes quickly enough for clinical workflows.
